title: What is the best AI tool for 3D character animation?
author: NothingHistorical322
selftext:
Hi everyone, I'm a solo developer making a mobile RTS game in Unity. I have several 3D warrior characters, but I don't have enough budget to hire a professional animator.

I need animations like **idle, walk, run, attack, hit reaction, and death**.

I'm thinking about using AI to create the animations and then import them into Unity.

What AI tools would you recommend for **good-quality 3D character animation**? I'm especially interested in something that works well with game characters, supports retargeting/export to Unity, and isn't too expensive.

I'd really appreciate recommendations from people who have actually used these tools.

comments.author: Officialpolygrafix
comments.body:
I've worked on quite a few RTS games. I do all the animations by hand.  
But i wanted to mention, keep your bone count low unless your min-spec is a really high end machine.   
I typically use a bones system rig in 3ds max and the hands and feet don't use all the bones hands and feet use.  I use 8 bones per hand and 1-2 bones per foot, 3 on the spine. When you have potentially hundreds of characters on the screen all animating at once, this is important.   Modern games usually use advanced rigs with med-high poly characters and lots of bones. I'm just throwing this out there to be cautious as you move foward.  
I don't have a good ai solution for rigging or bones system other than mixamo, but theres another i wanted to look into called casceduer, it looks promising for animation.

comments.author: w1a1s1p
comments.body: I took reference images from astra, sent them through the 3D studio process at tencent 3D (you get some free credits daily) and let astra optimize the files each turn through blender MCP

comments.author: Alternative-Shame147
comments.body: Why don't you want to use off-the-shelf animations for standard-rigged skeletons? There are quite a few available to suit various tastes. You could start with Mixamo.

comments.author: btspman1
comments.body: You can buy pre-made animations that you can load into your biped/bone structure. Probably cheaper than trial and error using AI

comments.author: Deelook
comments.body:
Since you already have the warrior models, Tripo might be worth trying for the rigging side too. You can auto-rig the character, add preset animations like idle/run/attack, then export the skeleton and animations with the FBX into Unity.

For an RTS I'd probably use that for the common animations first, then clean up or replace the more specific stuff like attacks and death animations if they don't look right. You don't really need every unit to have some super detailed custom animation set, especially if they're going to be fairly small on screen.

I'd test one warrior all the way into Unity first though. Make sure the rig, weights and animations behave properly before doing the rest of the characters.
